body: This may only be happening when both the table and one of its columns contain dashes.

Is this error happening with every DBAL version or just the one you mentioned above? As far as I see this happens with other DBAL versions too, right?

Because our builds don't contain Microsoft SQL-Server this is hard to fix and protect from regressions.

I haven't checked if this happens on other versions of the DBAL and I'm afraid I can't make an aducated guess.

As far as regression testing is concerned, isn't it possible to instantiate Doctrine with the SQLServer platform object (or other necessary collaborators) and generate the SQL statement without connecting to an actual database?

That wouldn't be an integration test but it would at least protect against regression with this bug.
Can you please show the full query that is resulting in this error in Microsoft SQL-Server?

I have a patch ready to fix this bug. Could someone please move this issue to the **doctrine/dbal** project so I can rename the test and open a pull-request there? 

Alternatively, would you rather I closed this bug report and opened a fresh one on the correct project?
Depending on the test this seems to be a DBAL issue. Thank you for staying involved in this.

issue.title: Fixes invalid T-SQL column comment for quoted table names.
issue.body:
<!-- Fill in the relevant information below to help triage your pull request. -->

|      Q           |   A
|------------- | -----------
| Type            | bug
| BC Break     | no
| Fixed issues | #4283 

#### Summary

<!-- Provide a summary of your change. -->

This merge request fixes the issue whereby a quoted table or schema name was getting converted into a string literal, resulting in a T-SQL statement referencing an invalid table name like `N'[table_name]'`. 

The issues happened whenever the entity table name contained [Quoted Reserved Words](https://www.doctrine-project.org/projects/doctrine-orm/en/2.7/reference/basic-mapping.html#quoting-reserved-words), for example:

```php
/**
 * @ORM\Table(name="`the-model-table`")
 */
class TheModel
{
}
```

The issue is fixed within the `SQLServer2012Platform` base class by inserting the schema or table names as T-SQL identifiers when generating the call to `sp_addextendedproperty` for quoted names. 

In other words, because Doctrine converts a quoted name like `` `table-name` `` into a valid T-SQL identifier like `[table-name]` we needn't wrap the identifier into a string literal before passing it to `getAddExtendedPropertySQL`.

issue.title: Fix identifier escaping when used as string literal for T-SQL
issue.body:
|      Q       |   A
|------------- | -----------
| Type         | bug
| BC Break     | no
| Fixed issues | #4283

#### Summary

Alternative to closes https://github.com/doctrine/dbal/pull/4284 to fix it correctly and with proper functional tests.

The issue was that MSSQL expects string literal (quoted by `'`) for `EXEC sp_addextendedproperty` instead of identifier name (quoted by `[]`).

issue.title: Fix SQL Server "extended property" SQL generation
issue.body:
|      Q       |   A
|------------- | -----------
| Type         | bug
| Fixed issues | #4283, superseeded #4360, #4585

#### Summary

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/system-stored-procedures/sp-addextendedproperty-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver15 shows the `sp_addextendedproperty` accepts `sysname` datatype which is subtype of string datatype and therefore the values must be escaped as string literal instead of escaped identifier. This is evident also in the [examples](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/system-stored-procedures/sp-addextendedproperty-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver15#examples).

As the DBAL method arguments accepts possibly escaped identifier, we unescape it before we escape the argument as string literal.
